The missing layer

            
Enforcement is only half the job.

          

          

            Latch enforces a policy. LatchLens asks the uncomfortable question:
            does the policy actually express what its owner meant?
          

        


        

          

            
01

            

              
            

            
Attack, not checklist

            

              It turns one pipeline into boundary cases: destructive verbs,
              endpoint confusion, token theft, cost bursts, PII egress and
              signer wildcard abuse.
            

          


          

            
02

            

              
            

            
Explain every denial

            

              Every scenario includes the ordered first-deny trace, so builders
              can distinguish real protection from accidental breakage.
            

          


          

            
03

            

              
            

            
Proof, not screenshots

            

              Reports are deterministically hashed and shaped for a Rialo
              attestation, turning a one-time test into portable evidence.
            

          

        

      


      

        

          
Rialo-native roadmap

          
Continuous assurance, without another keeper.

          

            Local analysis never needs a credential. Optional Live Latch Verify
            sends six safe hypothetical requests through a narrow Vercel adapter
            to Latch Authorize, then compares canonical decisions with the local
            mirror. A Rialo workflow can later detect drift and anchor only the
            report hash—not the private policy.
          

          

            Native timers
            Native HTTPS
            Reactive alerts

            MVP boundary
          

          

            Local results remain drafts until explicitly checked. Live verification
            is opt-in, labels skipped context-only cases, and never claims a Rialo
            anchor; the DevNet attestor still requires deployment.

          MVP boundary
          
            Local mode is credential-free. Live Latch mode uses a lat_ token
            transiently through the fixed adapter. DevNet anchoring is optional,
            owner-signed, and sends LatchLens only a public transaction signature.
          
        


        

          
          
        

      

    


    

      

        

          

            
Canonical comparison · opt-in

            
Verify with live Latch

          

          
        


        

          Compare the local mirror with the effective policy attached to your
          Latch token. Authorize returns decisions without calling the upstream
          or using its protected credential.
        


        

          

          

            Token boundary
            
              The token is sent over HTTPS to this site's Vercel Function, which
              forwards it only to Latch's fixed authorize endpoint. LatchLens code
              does not persist, log, echo or include it in reports. The input is
              cleared as soon as verification starts.
            
          


          

            

              6
              canonical requests
            

            

              8
              local context checks
            

            

              Identity, clock, rate, spend, response, delegation, signer and
              oversized-body scenarios remain local because Authorize cannot
              safely simulate that context.
            

          


          

            

              No Latch token yet?
              
                Your 14-case local proof is still complete. Live comparison is
                optional and can be added later.
